sections.heading: Updated October 22, 2026
sections.body:
The Arrow · Monsoon Isle

This policy explains what information we handle, why, and how you can manage it or request its deletion. This policy describes the privacy controls in this version of the game.

sections.heading: At a glance
sections.body:
The Arrow is intended for users aged 13 and over and needs no player account. Progress and settings are saved on your device.

Before playing, read the complete Privacy Policy and Terms of Use and choose Accept. Your saved acceptance covers the ordinary Firebase Analytics/GA4 gameplay statistics and Firebase Crashlytics Java/NDK reports described below. Advertising choices are handled separately by Google UMP. Declining advertising purposes does not cancel ordinary acceptance.

Clearing local data resets progress but does not automatically delete information already received by Google. For privacy questions or requests, email aquark314@gmail.com.

sections.heading: 1. Scope and responsibility
sections.body:
Monsoon Isle ("we", "us" or "our") develops The Arrow and is responsible for the processing described here for which we determine the purposes and means. This policy covers The Arrow for Android (package: com.monsoonisle.thearrow), related support communications, and the Monsoon Isle website described in section 11.

Personal information includes information that identifies you directly or together with other information. Device identifiers, installation identifiers and IP addresses may qualify even without your real name.

sections.heading: 2. Local and provided information
sections.body:
Game records on your device

The game saves settings, level progress, achievements, daily rewards, unfinished games and diagnostic records on your device to restore game state and run these features. After valid acceptance and the applicable recipient, age, storage and SDK checks, local analytics records can contain gameplay events and randomly generated installation, session and event identifiers. Our pending ordinary events are bounded to three days. Temporary document checks preserve previously eligible pending data; a new recipient or retired ordinary scope does not inherit that data. This version does not use the earlier default-on restricted-measurement scheme.

Local storage does not mean all related information stays on your device. Some progress, gameplay and advertising events are sent through the analytics service in section 3. This differs from uploading complete saved games or providing cloud saves.

Information you provide

When you email us, we receive your email address, message and any attachments you choose to send. We use them to respond, troubleshoot and handle your request. Please provide only necessary information and avoid sending passwords, payment details or unnecessary sensitive information.

The game needs no player account and does not ask for your name or contact details. It currently does not request access to precise device location, contacts, the camera or the microphone.

Necessary legal-document requests

Before acceptance, the app can retrieve these documents from monsoonisle.github.io without adding analytics, advertising or saved-game identifiers. GitHub Pages still receives network request metadata including your IP address. Verified complete bundled or saved documents are available offline when no newer applicable requirement is already known.

If you choose Share ad diagnostics, the app creates a small local status file and opens the Android share sheet. This basic file excludes installation/session/advertising identifiers and raw ad-response data. No recipient is selected and no file is automatically uploaded. Export files remain in app cache; on a later export the app removes older export files and limits their number. Clearing app cache removes these local export copies.

sections.heading: 3. Analytics, promotion and crash reports
sections.body:
The Arrow uses Google Analytics for Firebase/GA4 for ordinary product statistics after your explicit Privacy and Terms acceptance and the applicable technical and age checks. Events can include gameplay and ad activity; launches, session duration, level starts/results, progress, tutorials, hints and rewards; loading times and technical errors; event times, app version, device model, operating system and language; and random installation, session and event identifiers. Google can also process SDK app-instance identifiers and approximate geographic information. These identifiers can link events, so the information is not necessarily anonymous.

Advertising measurement is separate. Firebase advertising storage, advertising user data and advertising personalization follow their own actual UMP signals. Our custom ad-revenue and ad-identity records additionally require the relevant advertising-measurement purposes and the original advertising generation. Unknown or refused advertising purposes are not inferred from Accept or from permission to request an ad. A later advertising choice does not relabel old ad records or reset eligible ordinary gameplay statistics.

Crash reports

The same acceptance explicitly covers Firebase Crashlytics Java/NDK reports to investigate crashes, freezes and technical errors. Reports can include crash traces, native crash data, device and operating-system details, app version, diagnostic identifiers and, when analytics is enabled, preceding analytics events. We do not add your name, email address or complete saved game to crash reports. Automatic report upload remains disabled: eligible previous-session reports may be submitted on a later launch under the same accepted recipient scope. A temporary document check retains eligible reports; a different recipient scope requires separate SDK preparation. Already submitted or in-transit reports cannot be recalled by a local change.

Older optional analytics/crash switches and UMP publisher content/development purposes do not generate the new acceptance. This version has no separate ordinary-statistics or crash-sharing switch. Reading the documents, pressing Back, changing language or choosing an ad does not create acceptance.

sections.heading: 4. Advertising
sections.body:
The Arrow uses Google AdMob for rewarded and interstitial ads. You can choose to watch rewarded ads for an in-game benefit.

To deliver and measure ads and prevent fraud, Google's Mobile Ads SDK processes IP addresses and inferred approximate location, app and ad interactions, diagnostics such as performance information, and device or account identifiers such as advertising ID and app set ID. Processing depends on SDK version, configuration, device settings and applicable consent status. App set ID serves permitted purposes such as analytics and fraud prevention, not ad personalization.

Ad personalization depends on applicable consent, advertising configuration and device settings. Non-personalized ads can still involve data for delivery, frequency control, security and measurement. Watching a rewarded ad does not itself mean consenting to unrelated tracking or personalized advertising.

See the Google Privacy Policy and Google Mobile Ads SDK data disclosure. Section 8 describes your available choices.

sections.heading: 5. Purposes and legal bases
sections.body:
We handle the information described above to run and save game features; understand gameplay and fix problems; deliver and measure ads, evaluate and optimize game promotion, grant rewards and prevent abuse; respond to support and privacy requests; and meet applicable legal obligations.

Where a legal basis is required, processing necessary for game features and support you request is based on performing the relevant service agreement. Mandatory retention or disclosure is based on legal obligations. Where permitted and not overridden by your rights and interests, security, troubleshooting and service improvement may rely on corresponding legitimate interests.

Analytics, device information access or personalized advertising requiring consent must take place only after valid consent. Legitimate interests cannot replace legally required consent. You can request withdrawal under section 8. Reading this policy or continuing to play does not itself constitute consent to that processing.

The app records your explicit Accept for the complete, applicable Privacy Policy and Terms of Use set, including its revision, original-byte hashes, recipient scope and environment. This ordinary decision does not grant advertising purposes. Where a different legal basis or additional protection is required, this interface does not remove those requirements.

sections.heading: 6. Sharing and international processing
sections.body:
• Google: receives the information in sections 3 and 4 through Firebase Analytics, AdMob, Google Ads integrations and Firebase Crashlytics under the applicable service terms and privacy information.

• Hosting and communications providers: GitHub Pages hosts the website and email providers process support messages, each handling information needed for its functions.

• Legal and security needs: we may disclose information necessary to comply with applicable law, respond to lawful requests or protect users and services, limiting disclosure to what is reasonably necessary.

• Your instructions or consent: we provide additional notice and obtain consent where required before sharing personal information for other purposes.

We do not sell local saved-game files. Advertising data transfers may qualify as a "sale", "sharing" or targeted advertising under some laws; the statement about saved-game files does not mean such activities never occur. See section 8 for relevant rights.

Providers may process information outside your country, including in the United States, where data protection rules may differ. Required transfer mechanisms and safeguards must be used under applicable law. Provider privacy notices explain their locations and protections; you can also contact us about our processing activities.

sections.heading: 7. Retention and deletion
sections.body:
We use Google's analytics and advertising services and do not separately store raw gameplay analytics on servers we operate ourselves. Records on your device, Google-hosted data and support emails you send us remain subject to the following separate retention rules:

• Local saves and analytics records: the game saves progress, settings and local analytics records on your device until updated, overwritten or removed. Clear The Arrow's storage in Android settings or uninstall it to remove local data; this resets progress. Migration or backup services may keep separate copies that you need to manage through them.

• Firebase Analytics data: Google hosts this data. Our retention policy for applicable user-level and event-level analytics data is 2 months, with expired data removed through Google's scheduled deletion process. This period does not apply to standard aggregate reports, AdMob advertising data or local device records. See Google Analytics data retention.

• Firebase Crashlytics data: Google retains crash traces, extracted native crash data and associated identifiers for 90 days before beginning removal from live and backup systems. Native minidumps are held temporarily for processing. This is separate from the Analytics two-month setting. See Firebase privacy and security information.

• AdMob advertising data: Google retains this for purposes such as ad delivery, measurement and fraud prevention, under applicable policies and legal requirements. Periods can differ by data type and do not follow the Analytics retention setting. See Google's data retention information.

• Website hosting logs: GitHub retains these under its hosting service purposes, privacy statement and applicable law.

• Support correspondence: we keep it only as needed to resolve issues, follow up on requests and meet legal obligations, then delete or anonymize it when no longer needed.

Clearing app storage, uninstalling the game or deleting an advertising ID does not automatically erase information already sent to Google. For access to or deletion of information we can identify and control, contact us under section 8. We will explain any legal need to retain information and relevant limitations.

sections.heading: 8. Your choices and privacy rights
sections.body:
Privacy and advertising choices

Settings provides full Privacy Policy and Terms of Use reading and the advertising choices required by Google UMP. Manage options can save partial or no advertising consent when the official message offers those choices. Advertising controls do not withdraw your ordinary acceptance.

This version requires an explicitly saved acceptance before playing and has no separate ordinary-analytics or crash-sharing switch. Historical grants, refusals, missing records and damaged records do not count as the new acceptance; upgrading asks for a fresh explicit decision. You may close the game without accepting. To withdraw acceptance and stop subsequent in-app collection, stop using the app and clear its storage or uninstall; this also removes local progress and settings. This does not automatically delete information already received by providers. For applicable withdrawal, objection, access or deletion requests, contact us using the process below.

Android or Google settings also provide advertising privacy choices, including resetting or deleting advertising ID; those actions do not erase all data already collected.

Making a privacy request

Depending on applicable law, you may have rights to know about and access your information, obtain a copy, correct or delete it, restrict or object to processing, request data portability and withdraw consent. Withdrawal does not affect lawful processing based on prior consent. Some jurisdictions also provide rights to opt out of targeted advertising or the "sale" or "sharing" of information, appeal decisions and complain to a competent supervisory authority.

Users in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland can exercise applicable data protection rights described above and complain to a competent local data protection authority. US residents can request to opt out of the "sale" or "sharing" of personal information or targeted advertising where applicable state law provides these rights. Users in Southeast Asia and other regions can make requests under their applicable local laws; this policy does not limit those rights.

Email aquark314@gmail.com with the subject "The Arrow Privacy Request", the action you want, and helpful context such as your game version and approximate usage dates. We request additional information only as needed to verify the request, protect data or locate records. Please do not send identity documents or passwords unsolicited.

Without player accounts, a name or email usually cannot identify every installation or SDK record. If we cannot locate data or a provider independently controls it, we explain the limitation and provide relevant request channels where possible. We handle requests within applicable legal deadlines and explain extensions or refusals and available next steps. We will not treat you unfairly for lawfully exercising privacy rights.

sections.heading: 9. Children and younger users
sections.body:
The Arrow is intended for users aged 13 and over and is not directed to children under 13. Store content ratings (such as "3+") describe content suitability and are separate from the game's intended audience and privacy consent requirements.

Users aged 13 and over may still be minors protected by local law. Higher age thresholds or other requirements for data processing, parental consent or personalized advertising continue to apply where required. Reaching age 13 or meeting a store content rating does not replace required consent. Parents and guardians should consider this policy when managing a minor's use.

The game includes third-party ads and analytics that may process the technical information in sections 3 and 4. We do not ask for names or contact details in the game, but this does not mean that no personal information about minors is processed.

If you believe information about a child under 13 has been collected through the game, or a minor's information has been processed without legally required consent or protections, contact aquark314@gmail.com. Once verified, we will delete relevant information we can identify and control, restrict the related processing and help direct requests to service providers where needed.

sections.heading: 10. Information security
sections.body:
We take reasonable safeguards appropriate to the information and processing risks. Google's relevant SDKs use encrypted connections. Local records also depend on device and operating system access protections. No storage or transmission method guarantees absolute security.

Please protect your device and send only necessary support information through our designated contact channel. We will meet applicable notification requirements if a security incident requires notice.

sections.heading: 11. Website visits and external links
sections.body:
The Monsoon Isle website (monsoonisle.github.io) introduces games, publishes this policy and provides contact details. Our pages currently include no advertising or visitor analytics scripts, set no tracking cookies, and do not use browser local storage.

GitHub Pages hosts the site. GitHub logs visitors' IP addresses for security under its Privacy Statement. Having no analytics scripts of our own does not mean the host processes no visit records.

External websites, app stores and services handle information under their own policies. This policy describes our practices and does not replace third-party notices.

sections.heading: 12. Policy updates and contact
sections.body: We may update this policy as features, providers or requirements change. The app checks the applicable versioned Privacy Policy and Terms of Use together. An applicable new requirement is saved before downloading the new complete set; after current saves, settlements and rewards finish safely, a changed set requires a new explicit Accept before eligible play and ordinary sharing resume. A text-only reconfirmation under the same recipient scope retains that scope and eligible pending data; a different recipient scope does not inherit old records. Offline fallback does not claim knowledge of the latest online version. Policy publication alone does not grant consent or change your advertising purposes.
